source.title: Data optimization for large batch distributed training of deep neural networks
source.authors: Shubhankar Gahlot; Jun-Qi Yin; M. Shankar

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch size and a data-filtering intervention affect classification accuracy on CIFAR-10, using accuracy results as a conceptual test of generalization-gap behavior. It does not directly report training-versus-test error gaps.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own CIFAR-10 batch-size results and its comparison of filtered, full, and randomly filtered training data. The figures' exact batch-size curves are not recoverable from text, so no values were inferred from them. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5 in CIFAR-10 ResNets: with training held at 50 epochs, accuracy declines beyond a preferred batch size. Held-out accuracy suffices to test V5; a training–test gap is not required. The filtering comparisons alone do not establish whether filtering reduces the large-versus-small-batch penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report an optimal batch-size range, better filtered-data accuracy at certain batch sizes above about 6k, similar accuracy below 6k, and better DDP scaling than Horovod. Smoothing the loss landscape is their proposed explanation, not a directly measured result.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CIFAR-10 ResNets and examines batch-size scaling plus t-SNE/DBSCAN training-data filtering. The cited large-batch studies are background; the paper's own filtered-data intervention is different from their training-recipe adjustments.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and learning rate change the accuracy pattern; the relative outcome also varies with full, network-filtered, and randomly filtered training data and weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-space filtering improves ResNet-18 accuracy over random filtering, improves over full-data training at reported batch sizes above about 6k, and produces similar accuracy below 6k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing examples classified as feature-space noise can preserve or improve held-out accuracy; this does not establish that filtering closes the large-batch penalty or removes highly memorized examples.

record.peer_reviewed: 2020 International Conference on Computational Science and Computational Intelligence (CSCI)
record.problems: The paper reports accuracy rather than a direct training-test gap; batch-size curve values and numerical error bars are only shown in figures. The data-filtering comparisons use different weight decays in some conditions, limiting attribution of differences to filtering alone. Results are on CIFAR-10 ResNets.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for batch-size curve points or network sizes in Figures 5 and 7 because exact values are figure-only and not stated in the text. Communication-scaling results compare distributed libraries and do not measure a version's generalization claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy versus natural-label training.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and tuning conditions.

Language models; longer training; learning-rate scaling with warmup; controlled normalization or regularization remedies; and whether filtering restores small-batch accuracy or reduces the large-versus-small-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of examples selected by memorization influence versus equally sized random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Additional architecture-specific batch-size results are already declared in rows_left_out. Figure-only values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance are not compared.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison is reported.
No adaptive optimizer comparison is reported.

Reports CIFAR-10 ResNet accuracy across batch sizes and a data-filtering intervention, but does not directly measure the training-test generalization gap or compare language models. It does not establish results for fixed epoch budgets across all conditions in the version.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measure is evaluated.
No memorized-example removal comparison is reported.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on full CIFAR-10 data for 50 epochs with SGD across batch sizes; accuracy varied with batch size and learning rate.
rows.value: Accuracy is not linearly correlated with batch size; there is a preferred batch size for each tested learning rate, beyond which accuracy drops gradually.
rows.note: The text describes the pattern across ResNet models; this row records the stated ResNet-18 result. Exact curve values are only in figures.
rows.check: The reported decline beyond the optimal batch size directly matches V5, rather than showing only a partial effect. Section IV.A describes multiple ResNet architectures; the gradual decline is explicitly attributed to ResNet-18 and ResNet-34.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared Network filtered, Full, and Randomly filtered CIFAR-10 training data across distributed large batch sizes.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a large-batch accuracy result; it does not give training accuracy or a generalization-gap value.
rows.check: The 77.5% versus 75.2% comparison establishes a filtering benefit at batch size 6272, not recovery of small-batch accuracy. The large-batch weight decay is internally inconsistent: Section IV.B specifies 0.01, whereas IV.B.1 says 0.005 was selected.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared Network filtered, Full, and Randomly filtered CIFAR-10 training data across distributed large batch sizes.
rows.measure: top-1 accuracy relative to Full data
rows.value: Network filtered data consistently achieves higher top-1 accuracy than Full data
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the stated range; no per-batch values are given in text.
rows.check: Higher accuracy after filtering at large batch sizes does not by itself establish a reduced batch-size penalty. The stated large-batch weight decay is internally inconsistent.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared Network filtered, Full, and Randomly filtered CIFAR-10 training data across distributed batch sizes.
rows.measure: top-1 accuracy relative to Full data
rows.value: Network filtered data accuracy is well within the error bars of Full data; authors conclude accuracy is similar
rows.uncertainty: error bars are referenced but not numerically stated
rows.note: The paper describes similarity within error bars, not an exact numeric difference.
rows.check: Similarity between filtered and full datasets below 6k measures the filtering effect, not absence of a batch-size penalty. The filtering benefit is absent within the reported error bars.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 trained with SGD for 50 epochs, beyond the preferred batch size at the tested learning rates
relationships.reason: R1 reports declining accuracy as batch size increases beyond its optimum, matching the fixed-epoch large-batch penalty.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy declined beyond the batch size that gave the best accuracy within a fixed epoch budget, but this comparison remains unverified.
